newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel sticking to strict EMU criteria - ministry.
newsitem.headline: Waigel sticking to strict EMU criteria - ministry.

text.p: The German Finance Ministry denied reports on Monday that Finance Minister Theo Waigel had moved to a more lenient interpretation of the three percent budget deficit limit set down as a criterion for European monetary union.
"The minister's position has not changed in the slightest," a ministry spokeswoman said. "He is sticking to his strict interpretation of the Maastricht qualification criteria for monetary union."
She said this had also been Waigel's position at the weekend meeting of EU Finance Ministers in the Netherlands.
Waigel has repeatedly insisted that he takes the three percent limit on budget deficits to mean 3.0 percent of Gross Domestic Product and no more.

Two British dailies, the Guardian and the Financial Times, reported from the meeting that Waigel had shifted his stance, quoting him as saying: "I have never nailed myself to the cross of three percent".
The Guardian quoted Irish Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn saying the words were "probably the most important which have been said during the weekend".
